answer: Constant-round MPC evaluates any function in a fixed number of rounds regardless of circuit depth, and the anchor of the design is garbled circuits with precomputed input labels. The fable of the protocol is that the round count does not leak the complexity of the check, so an identity test over a large list runs as fast as a small one. A Sybil farm cannot delay or stall the computation because the rounds are fixed, and the inlet of the design keeps latency predictable for real-time verification.
